import Definitions.Def_FermatCurveFieldChart
import Mathlib.RingTheory.DedekindDomain.AdicValuation
import Mathlib.RingTheory.DedekindDomain.Dvr
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Valuation.Discrete.IsDiscreteValuationRing

/-!
# Places of a curve field

A *place* of a field `K` is a valuation subring `O ⊊ K` containing `ℚ` (the condition
`ℚ ⊆ O` excludes e.g. the Gauss extension of a `p`-adic valuation of `ℚ` to `ℚ(t)`).
For a curve field `K` (`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.IsCurveField`) the places are the closed points of
the regular proper model of the curve, and they are described by the affine *charts*
`A_t = chartRing t`: for `t` transcendental, the places containing `t` are exactly the
localisations of the Dedekind domain `A_t` at its height-one primes
(`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.chartEquiv`); every place contains `t` or `t⁻¹`.

## Main definitions

* `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place K`: the places of `K`.
* `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.ord P : K → ℤ`: the normalised discrete valuation at `P`
  (with the junk value `ord 0 = 0`).
* `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.ResidueField P`: the residue field, a number field.
* `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.deg P`: the degree `[κ(P) : ℚ]`.
* `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.chartEquiv t`: places containing `t` ≃ height-one primes of `A_t`.

## Main results

* `IsDiscreteValuationRing P.1`; the valuation laws for `ord`; uniformisers.
* `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.finite_setOf_ord_ne_zero`,
  `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.finite_setOf_notMem`: finiteness of zeros and poles.
* `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.exists_ord_pos`, `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.exists_ord_neg`: a
  transcendental element has a zero and a pole;
  `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.isAlgebraic_of_forall_mem`: an element lying in every place is
  algebraic over `ℚ`.
-/

open IsDedekindDomain IsLocalRing
open scoped IntermediateField WithZero

namespace AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper

section Abstract

/-! ### Valuation subrings dominating a Dedekind domain -/

variable {K : Type*} [Field K]
variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [Algebra R K]

/-- The prime of `R` lying below a valuation subring `O` containing (the image of) `R`. -/
def primeBelow (O : ValuationSubring K) (hR : ∀ r, algebraMap R K r ∈ O) : Ideal R :=
  (maximalIdeal O).comap ((algebraMap R K).codRestrict O hR)

theorem mem_primeBelow {O : ValuationSubring K} {hR : ∀ r, algebraMap R K r ∈ O} {r : R} :
    r ∈ primeBelow O hR ↔ algebraMap R K r ∈ O.nonunits := by
  rw [primeBelow, Ideal.mem_comap, ← ValuationSubring.coe_mem_nonunits_iff]
  rfl

instance (O : ValuationSubring K) (hR : ∀ r, algebraMap R K r ∈ O) :
    (primeBelow O hR).IsPrime := Ideal.comap_isPrime _ _

section Domain

variable [IsDomain R]

theorem primeBelow_ne_bot [IsFractionRing R K] {O : ValuationSubring K} (hO : O ≠ ⊤)
    (hR : ∀ r, algebraMap R K r ∈ O) : primeBelow O hR ≠ ⊥ := by
  intro h
  apply hO
  refine top_unique fun x _ ↦ ?_
  obtain ⟨a, b, hb, rfl⟩ := IsFractionRing.div_surjective (A := R) x
  have hb0 : algebraMap R K b ≠ 0 :=
    IsFractionRing.to_map_ne_zero_of_mem_nonZeroDivisors hb
  have hbn : algebraMap R K b ∉ O.nonunits := by
    rw [← mem_primeBelow (hR := hR), h, Ideal.mem_bot]
    exact fun h0 ↦ hb0 (by rw [h0, map_zero])
  rw [ValuationSubring.mem_nonunits_iff_or, not_or, not_not] at hbn
  rw [div_eq_mul_inv]
  exact O.mul_mem _ _ (hR a) hbn.2

/-- The height-one prime of `R` below a valuation subring `O ≠ K` containing `R`. -/
def heightOneBelow [IsFractionRing R K] (O : ValuationSubring K) (hO : O ≠ ⊤)
    (hR : ∀ r, algebraMap R K r ∈ O) : HeightOneSpectrum R :=
  ⟨primeBelow O hR, inferInstance, primeBelow_ne_bot hO hR⟩

theorem mem_heightOneBelow [IsFractionRing R K] {O : ValuationSubring K} {hO : O ≠ ⊤}
    {hR : ∀ r, algebraMap R K r ∈ O} {r : R} :
    r ∈ (heightOneBelow O hO hR).asIdeal ↔ algebraMap R K r ∈ O.nonunits :=
  mem_primeBelow

end Domain

variable [IsDedekindDomain R] [IsFractionRing R K]

theorem valuationSubringAtPrime_le (O : ValuationSubring K) (hO : O ≠ ⊤)
    (hR : ∀ r, algebraMap R K r ∈ O) :
    HeightOneSpectrum.valuationSubringAtPrime K (heightOneBelow O hO hR) ≤ O := by
  rintro x ⟨a, s, hs, rfl⟩
  have hsn : algebraMap R K s ∉ O.nonunits := by
    rw [← mem_primeBelow (hR := hR)]; exact hs
  rw [ValuationSubring.mem_nonunits_iff_or, not_or, not_not] at hsn
  exact O.mul_mem _ _ (hR a) hsn.2

/-- A valuation subring `O ≠ K` containing a Dedekind domain `R` with fraction field `K` is
the localisation of `R` at the prime below `O`. -/
theorem valuationSubringAtPrime_heightOneBelow (O : ValuationSubring K) (hO : O ≠ ⊤)
    (hR : ∀ r, algebraMap R K r ∈ O) :
    HeightOneSpectrum.valuationSubringAtPrime K (heightOneBelow O hO hR) = O :=
  ValuationSubring.eq_of_le_of_ne_top _ (valuationSubringAtPrime_le O hO hR) hO

instance (v : HeightOneSpectrum R) :
    IsDiscreteValuationRing (HeightOneSpectrum.valuationSubringAtPrime K v) :=
  IsLocalization.AtPrime.isDiscreteValuationRing_of_dedekind_domain R v.ne_bot _

theorem isDiscreteValuationRing_of_le (O : ValuationSubring K) (hO : O ≠ ⊤)
    (hR : ∀ r, algebraMap R K r ∈ O) : IsDiscreteValuationRing O := by
  rw [← valuationSubringAtPrime_heightOneBelow O hO hR]; infer_instance

theorem valuationSubringAtPrime_ne_top (v : HeightOneSpectrum R) :
    HeightOneSpectrum.valuationSubringAtPrime K v ≠ ⊤ := by
  rw [HeightOneSpectrum.valuationSubringAtPrime_eq_valuationSubring, ne_eq,
    Valuation.valuationSubring_eq_top_iff, not_not]
  infer_instance

theorem algebraMap_mem_valuationSubringAtPrime (v : HeightOneSpectrum R) (r : R) :
    algebraMap R K r ∈ HeightOneSpectrum.valuationSubringAtPrime K v := by
  rw [HeightOneSpectrum.valuationSubringAtPrime_eq_valuationSubring,
    Valuation.mem_valuationSubring_iff]
  exact HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_le_one _ _

theorem heightOneBelow_valuationSubringAtPrime (v : HeightOneSpectrum R) :
    heightOneBelow (HeightOneSpectrum.valuationSubringAtPrime K v)
      (valuationSubringAtPrime_ne_top v) (algebraMap_mem_valuationSubringAtPrime v) = v := by
  ext r
  rw [mem_heightOneBelow, ValuationSubring.mem_nonunits_iff,
    ← HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_lt_one_iff_mem (K := K),
    HeightOneSpectrum.valuationSubringAtPrime_eq_valuationSubring]
  exact (Valuation.isEquiv_valuation_valuationSubring _).symm.lt_one_iff_lt_one

/-- The residue map of `O` restricted to a Dedekind domain `R ⊆ O` with fraction field `K`
is surjective (the residue field of `O` is `R ⧸ 𝔭`). -/
theorem residue_comp_surjective (O : ValuationSubring K) (hO : O ≠ ⊤)
    (hR : ∀ r, algebraMap R K r ∈ O) :
    Function.Surjective ((residue O).comp ((algebraMap R K).codRestrict O hR)) := by
  intro y
  obtain ⟨⟨x, hxO⟩, rfl⟩ := residue_surjective y
  have hx := hxO
  rw [← valuationSubringAtPrime_heightOneBelow O hO hR] at hx
  obtain ⟨a, s, hs, hxas⟩ := hx
  obtain ⟨b, i, hi, hbi⟩ := (heightOneBelow O hO hR).isMaximal.exists_inv hs
  refine ⟨a * b, ?_⟩
  rw [RingHom.comp_apply, eq_comm, ← sub_eq_zero, ← map_sub, residue_eq_zero_iff,
    ← ValuationSubring.coe_mem_nonunits_iff]
  have hs0 : algebraMap R K s ≠ 0 := by
    intro h0
    apply hs
    rw [(IsFractionRing.injective R K) (h0.trans (map_zero _).symm)]
    exact Ideal.zero_mem _
  have hin : algebraMap R K i ∈ O.nonunits := mem_heightOneBelow.mp hi
  have key : x - algebraMap R K (a * b) = x * algebraMap R K i := by
    have hbi' : algebraMap R K b * algebraMap R K s + algebraMap R K i = 1 := by
      rw [← map_mul, ← map_add, hbi, map_one]
    rw [hxas, map_mul, show algebraMap R K i = 1 - algebraMap R K b * algebraMap R K s by
      rw [← hbi']; ring]
    field_simp
  change x - algebraMap R K (a * b) ∈ O.nonunits
  rw [key, ValuationSubring.mem_nonunits_iff, map_mul]
  rw [ValuationSubring.mem_nonunits_iff] at hin
  calc O.valuation x * O.valuation (algebraMap R K i) < 1 * 1 :=
        mul_lt_mul_of_le_of_lt_of_nonneg_of_pos ((O.valuation_le_one_iff x).mpr hxO) hin
          zero_le zero_lt_one
    _ = 1 := one_mul 1

end Abstract

/-! ### Places -/

/- The actual Place carrier is already defined in Def_FermatProperCarrier. -/

namespace Place

variable {K : Type*} [Field K]

@[ext]
theorem ext {P Q : Place K} (h : P.1 = Q.1) : P = Q := Subtype.ext h

theorem ne_top (P : Place K) : P.1 ≠ ⊤ := P.2.1

theorem ratCast_mem (P : Place K) (q : ℚ) : (q : K) ∈ P.1 := P.2.2 q

theorem mem_or_inv_mem (P : Place K) (x : K) : x ∈ P.1 ∨ x⁻¹ ∈ P.1 := P.1.mem_or_inv_mem x

variable [CharZero K]

theorem algebraMap_mem (P : Place K) (q : ℚ) : algebraMap ℚ K q ∈ P.1 := P.ratCast_mem q

/-- Elements of `K` integral over `ℚ` (the constants) lie in every place. -/
theorem mem_of_isIntegral (P : Place K) {x : K} (hx : IsIntegral ℚ x) : x ∈ P.1 := by
  have : IsIntegrallyClosedIn P.1.toSubring K := inferInstanceAs (IsIntegrallyClosedIn P.1 K)
  have hle : (integralClosure ℚ K).toSubring ≤ P.1.toSubring :=
    Subring.integralClosure_le_iff.mpr P.algebraMap_mem
  exact hle hx

theorem mem_of_isAlgebraic (P : Place K) {x : K} (hx : IsAlgebraic ℚ x) : x ∈ P.1 :=
  P.mem_of_isIntegral hx.isIntegral

theorem inv_mem_of_isAlgebraic (P : Place K) {x : K} (hx : IsAlgebraic ℚ x) : x⁻¹ ∈ P.1 :=
  P.mem_of_isAlgebraic hx.inv

/-! ### Charts -/

section Chart

variable [IsCurveField K] (t : K) [Fact (Transcendental ℚ t)]

omit [IsCurveField K] [Fact (Transcendental ℚ t)] in
theorem algebraMap_chartRing_mem (P : Place K) (ht : t ∈ P.1) (r : chartRing t) :
    algebraMap (chartRing t) K r ∈ P.1 :=
  mem_of_mem_chartRing P.1 P.ratCast_mem ht r.2

/-- The height-one prime of the chart ring `A_t` below a place containing `t`. -/
noncomputable def toChart (P : Place K) (ht : t ∈ P.1) : HeightOneSpectrum (chartRing t) :=
  heightOneBelow P.1 P.ne_top (P.algebraMap_chartRing_mem t ht)

theorem mem_toChart_iff (P : Place K) (ht : t ∈ P.1) {r : chartRing t} :
    r ∈ (P.toChart t ht).asIdeal ↔ (r : K) ∈ P.1.nonunits :=
  mem_heightOneBelow

/-- The place of `K` given by the localisation of `A_t` at a height-one prime. -/
noncomputable def ofChart (v : HeightOneSpectrum (chartRing t)) : Place K :=
  ⟨HeightOneSpectrum.valuationSubringAtPrime K v, valuationSubringAtPrime_ne_top v,
    fun q ↦ algebraMap_mem_valuationSubringAtPrime v ⟨q, ratCast_mem_chartRing t q⟩⟩

theorem ofChart_val (v : HeightOneSpectrum (chartRing t)) :
    (ofChart t v).1 = HeightOneSpectrum.valuationSubringAtPrime K v := rfl

theorem self_mem_ofChart (v : HeightOneSpectrum (chartRing t)) : t ∈ (ofChart t v).1 :=
  algebraMap_mem_valuationSubringAtPrime v ⟨t, self_mem_chartRing t⟩

@[simp]
theorem ofChart_toChart (P : Place K) (ht : t ∈ P.1) : ofChart t (P.toChart t ht) = P :=
  Place.ext (valuationSubringAtPrime_heightOneBelow _ _ _)

@[simp]
theorem toChart_ofChart (v : HeightOneSpectrum (chartRing t)) :
    (ofChart t v).toChart t (self_mem_ofChart t v) = v :=
  heightOneBelow_valuationSubringAtPrime v

/-- The places containing `t` correspond to the height-one primes of the chart ring `A_t`
(the place is the localisation of `A_t` at the prime). -/
noncomputable def chartEquiv : {P : Place K // t ∈ P.1} ≃ HeightOneSpectrum (chartRing t) where
  toFun P := P.1.toChart t P.2
  invFun v := ⟨ofChart t v, self_mem_ofChart t v⟩
  left_inv P := Subtype.ext (ofChart_toChart t P.1 P.2)
  right_inv v := toChart_ofChart t v

theorem residue_comp_surjective (P : Place K) (ht : t ∈ P.1) :
    Function.Surjective ((IsLocalRing.residue P.1).comp
      ((algebraMap (chartRing t) K).codRestrict P.1 (P.algebraMap_chartRing_mem t ht))) :=
  AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.residue_comp_surjective P.1 P.ne_top _

end Chart

section DVR

variable [IsCurveField K]

/-- Every place contains a transcendental element (namely `t` or `t⁻¹` for any
transcendental `t`). -/
theorem exists_transcendental_mem (P : Place K) : ∃ t : K, Transcendental ℚ t ∧ t ∈ P.1 := by
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := exists_transcendental K
  rcases P.mem_or_inv_mem t with h | h
  · exact ⟨t, ht, h⟩
  · exact ⟨t⁻¹, transcendental_inv ht, h⟩

instance isDiscreteValuationRing (P : Place K) : IsDiscreteValuationRing P.1 := by
  obtain ⟨t, ht, htP⟩ := P.exists_transcendental_mem
  have : Fact (Transcendental ℚ t) := ⟨ht⟩
  exact isDiscreteValuationRing_of_le P.1 P.ne_top (P.algebraMap_chartRing_mem t htP)

/-- The normalised discrete valuation of `K` at the place `P`, with values in `ℤᵐ⁰`. -/
noncomputable def valuation (P : Place K) : Valuation K ℤᵐ⁰ :=
  (IsDiscreteValuationRing.maximalIdeal P.1).valuation K

/-- The order of vanishing `ord_P f ∈ ℤ` of `f` at the place `P` (junk value `ord_P 0 = 0`). -/
noncomputable def ord (P : Place K) (f : K) : ℤ := -WithZero.log (P.valuation f)

variable (P : Place K) {f g : K}

@[simp]
theorem valuation_eq_zero_iff : P.valuation f = 0 ↔ f = 0 := Valuation.zero_iff _

theorem valuation_ne_zero (hf : f ≠ 0) : P.valuation f ≠ 0 := by simpa using hf

theorem valuation_eq_exp (hf : f ≠ 0) : P.valuation f = WithZero.exp (-P.ord f) := by
  rw [ord, neg_neg, WithZero.exp_log (P.valuation_ne_zero hf)]

@[simp]
theorem ord_zero : P.ord 0 = 0 := by simp [ord]

@[simp]
theorem ord_one : P.ord 1 = 0 := by simp [ord]

theorem ord_mul (hf : f ≠ 0) (hg : g ≠ 0) : P.ord (f * g) = P.ord f + P.ord g := by
  simp only [ord, map_mul, WithZero.log_mul (P.valuation_ne_zero hf) (P.valuation_ne_zero hg)]
  ring

@[simp]
theorem ord_inv (f : K) : P.ord f⁻¹ = -P.ord f := by
  simp [ord, map_inv₀, WithZero.log_inv]

@[simp]
theorem ord_pow (f : K) (n : ℕ) : P.ord (f ^ n) = n * P.ord f := by
  simp [ord, map_pow, WithZero.log_pow]

@[simp]
theorem ord_zpow (f : K) (n : ℤ) : P.ord (f ^ n) = n * P.ord f := by
  simp [ord, map_zpow₀, WithZero.log_zpow]

theorem ord_div (hf : f ≠ 0) (hg : g ≠ 0) : P.ord (f / g) = P.ord f - P.ord g := by
  rw [div_eq_mul_inv, P.ord_mul hf (inv_ne_zero hg), ord_inv, sub_eq_add_neg]

@[simp]
theorem ord_neg (f : K) : P.ord (-f) = P.ord f := by simp [ord]

theorem mem_iff_valuation_le_one : f ∈ P.1 ↔ P.valuation f ≤ 1 := by
  have := IsDiscreteValuationRing.map_algebraMap_eq_valuationSubring (A := P.1) (K := K)
  change _ ↔ f ∈ (P.valuation.valuationSubring.toSubring)
  rw [valuation, ← this]
  simp

theorem mem_iff_ord_nonneg : f ∈ P.1 ↔ f = 0 ∨ 0 ≤ P.ord f := by
  rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hf
  · simp [P.1.zero_mem]
  rw [mem_iff_valuation_le_one, P.valuation_eq_exp hf, ← WithZero.exp_zero, WithZero.exp_le_exp]
  simp [hf]

theorem ord_nonneg_of_mem (hf : f ∈ P.1) : 0 ≤ P.ord f := by
  rcases (P.mem_iff_ord_nonneg).mp hf with rfl | h
  · simp
  · exact h

theorem mem_of_ord_nonneg (hf : 0 ≤ P.ord f) : f ∈ P.1 :=
  (P.mem_iff_ord_nonneg).mpr (Or.inr hf)

theorem ord_neg_iff : P.ord f < 0 ↔ f ∉ P.1 := by
  rw [P.mem_iff_ord_nonneg, not_or, not_le]
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨fun h0 ↦ ?_, h⟩
    subst h0
    simp at h
  · exact fun h ↦ h.2

/-- For `a ∈ O_P` nonzero, `ord_P a > 0` iff `a` lies in the maximal ideal. -/
theorem ord_pos_iff_mem_maximalIdeal {a : P.1} (ha : (a : K) ≠ 0) :
    0 < P.ord a ↔ a ∈ maximalIdeal P.1 := by
  have h := HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_lt_one_iff_mem
    (IsDiscreteValuationRing.maximalIdeal P.1) (K := K) a
  change P.valuation a < 1 ↔ a ∈ maximalIdeal P.1 at h
  rw [← h, P.valuation_eq_exp ha, ← WithZero.exp_zero, WithZero.exp_lt_exp, Left.neg_neg_iff]

theorem ord_pos_iff : 0 < P.ord f ↔ f ≠ 0 ∧ f ∈ P.1.nonunits := by
  rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hf
  · simp
  simp only [ne_eq, hf, not_false_eq_true, true_and]
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hm : f ∈ P.1 := P.mem_of_ord_nonneg h.le
    have := (P.ord_pos_iff_mem_maximalIdeal (a := ⟨f, hm⟩) hf).mp h
    exact ValuationSubring.coe_mem_nonunits_iff.mpr this
  · intro h
    have hm : f ∈ P.1 := P.1.nonunits_subset h
    exact (P.ord_pos_iff_mem_maximalIdeal (a := ⟨f, hm⟩) hf).mpr
      (ValuationSubring.coe_mem_nonunits_iff.mp h)

theorem ord_eq_zero_iff (hf : f ≠ 0) : P.ord f = 0 ↔ f ∈ P.1 ∧ f⁻¹ ∈ P.1 := by
  rw [P.mem_iff_ord_nonneg, P.mem_iff_ord_nonneg, ord_inv]
  simp only [hf, inv_eq_zero, false_or, Left.nonneg_neg_iff]
  omega

theorem min_le_ord_add (hfg : f + g ≠ 0) : min (P.ord f) (P.ord g) ≤ P.ord (f + g) := by
  rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hf
  · simp
  rcases eq_or_ne g 0 with rfl | hg
  · simp
  have h := P.valuation.map_add f g
  rw [P.valuation_eq_exp hf, P.valuation_eq_exp hg, P.valuation_eq_exp hfg] at h
  rcases le_total (P.ord f) (P.ord g) with hle | hle
  · rw [max_eq_left (WithZero.exp_le_exp.mpr (neg_le_neg hle)), WithZero.exp_le_exp] at h
    rw [min_eq_left hle]; omega
  · rw [max_eq_right (WithZero.exp_le_exp.mpr (neg_le_neg hle)), WithZero.exp_le_exp] at h
    rw [min_eq_right hle]; omega

theorem ord_add_eq_of_lt (hf : f ≠ 0) (hg : g ≠ 0) (h : P.ord f < P.ord g) :
    P.ord (f + g) = P.ord f := by
  have hv : P.valuation g < P.valuation f := by
    rw [P.valuation_eq_exp hf, P.valuation_eq_exp hg, WithZero.exp_lt_exp]; omega
  have := P.valuation.map_add_eq_of_lt_left hv
  rw [ord, ord, this]

/-- Every place has a uniformiser. -/
theorem exists_ord_eq_one : ∃ π : K, P.ord π = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨π, hπ⟩ := HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_exists_uniformizer K
    (IsDiscreteValuationRing.maximalIdeal P.1)
  refine ⟨π, ?_⟩
  change -WithZero.log (P.valuation π) = 1
  rw [show P.valuation π = WithZero.exp (-1) from hπ, WithZero.log_exp, neg_neg]

/-- Constants (elements algebraic over `ℚ`) have order `0` at every place. -/
theorem ord_eq_zero_of_isAlgebraic {c : K} (hc : IsAlgebraic ℚ c) : P.ord c = 0 := by
  rcases eq_or_ne c 0 with rfl | hc0
  · simp
  exact (P.ord_eq_zero_iff hc0).mpr ⟨P.mem_of_isAlgebraic hc, P.inv_mem_of_isAlgebraic hc⟩

@[simp]
theorem ord_ratCast (q : ℚ) : P.ord (q : K) = 0 :=
  P.ord_eq_zero_of_isAlgebraic (isAlgebraic_algebraMap (R := ℚ) q)

@[simp]
theorem ord_algebraMap_rat (q : ℚ) : P.ord (algebraMap ℚ K q) = 0 := P.ord_ratCast q

@[simp]
theorem ord_natCast (n : ℕ) : P.ord (n : K) = 0 := by
  simpa using P.ord_ratCast n

/-- Elements of an algebraic extension `F` of `ℚ` inside `K` (constants) have order `0`. -/
theorem ord_algebraMap {F : Type*} [Field F] [CharZero F] [Algebra F K]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic ℚ F] (c : F) : P.ord (algebraMap F K c) = 0 :=
  P.ord_eq_zero_of_isAlgebraic
    ((Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isAlgebraic (R := ℚ) c).algHom (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom ℚ F K))

end DVR

end Place

end AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper

nodes.theorem_title: Canonical and Belyi cusp divisors are linearly equivalent to the polar divisor
nodes.formal_statement:
theorem AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.canonicalCuspPolarLinearEquivalence : ∀ {N : ℕ} (M : AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Model N) (hDVR : AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.PlacesDiscrete M),
  AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.ResiduesFinite M →
    ∀ (φ : ↥M.K),
      AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.IsBelyi M hDVR φ →
        ∀ (hfin : (AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.cusps M hDVR φ).Finite)
          (K : AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.CanonicalDivisorData M hDVR),
          ∃ (r : ↥M.K),
            r ≠ 0 ∧
              ∀ (P : AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place ↥M.K),
                K.D P + (AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.cuspDivisor M hDVR φ hfin) P =
                  AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.poleMultiplicity M hDVR φ P +
                    AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.ord M hDVR P r := by sorry

Shinichi Mochizuki, *Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position*, February 2009.

Official PDF: https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Arithmetic%20Elliptic%20Curves%20in%20General%20Position.pdf

Local PDF: `/home/admin-wsl/Coq/abc/refer/Mochizuki/Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position.pdf`

SHA-256: `b9dc115af61dca7fe434332ebafddf6a376a9e2926dad4e1ea2dcc0d2441f768`

Theorem 2.1(i) — printed page 11 / PDF page 11:

> Write $\omega_X$ for the canonical sheaf on $X$. Suppose that $U_X$ is a hyperbolic curve — i.e., that the degree of the line bundle $\omega_X(D)$ is positive.

Theorem 2.1(ii), opening clauses — printed page 11 / PDF page 11:

> Let $P \overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \mathbb{P}^1_{\mathbb{Q}}$ be the projective line over $\mathbb{Q}$; $C \subseteq P$ the divisor consisting of the three points “0”, “1”, and “$\infty$”;

A selected opening clause; the original sentence continues with further data.

Proof of Theorem 2.1 — printed page 12 / PDF page 12:

> Now set $E \overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \phi^{-1}(C)_{\mathrm{red}} \subseteq X$ [so $\phi^*\omega_P(C) \cong \omega_X(E)$].

These quotations give the original-paper canonical and log-canonical context. The arbitrary-transcendental differential-change statement and the explicit Belyi coefficient identity are exact formal-source auxiliaries from Belyi/CurveField/Canonical.lean:144,159 and BelyiRelation.lean:85; they are not quoted verbatim from this paper. The current statements retain every supplied canonical divisor and cusp-finiteness proof and all proper places, including poles. The formal source uses positive principal orders in this geometric composition.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.canonicalCuspPolarLinearEquivalence`

Let $N\in\mathbb N$ be the implicit parameter, and let the explicit model $M$ consist of an intermediate field $F$ over $\mathbb Q$ in the fixed algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbb Q(T)}$, elements $u,v\in F$, and proofs that $u$ is transcendental over $\mathbb Q$, $u^N+v^N=1$, $\mathbb Q(u,v)=F$, and $F/\mathbb Q(u)$ is finite-dimensional of degree $N$. There is no separate lower-bound hypothesis on $N$; a model with these properties cannot have $N=0$. A place $P$ means any valuation subring $O_P\subsetneq F$ containing $\mathbb Q$, with residue field $\kappa(P)=O_P/\mathfrak m_P$ and residue map $\rho_P$. The explicit hypotheses $h_{\mathrm{DVR}}$ and $h_{\mathrm{RF}}$ assert, respectively, that every such $O_P$ is a discrete valuation ring and that every $\kappa(P)$ is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb Q$. Write $\nu_P(f)$ for the normalized integer order obtained as minus the discrete logarithm of the maximal-ideal valuation supplied by $O_P$, whose value group is the multiplicative copy of $\mathbb Z$ with an adjoined zero; its totalized value is $\nu_P(0)=0$. For any $f\in F$, put $e_f(P)=\nu_P(m_{\rho_P(f)}(f))$ when $f\in O_P$, where $m_{\rho_P(f)}\in\mathbb Q[X]$ is the minimal polynomial over $\mathbb Q$ of the residue of $f$; when $f\notin O_P$, put $e_f(P)=-\nu_P(f)$. Define $a_f(P)=e_f(P)-1$ in the first branch and $a_f(P)=-e_f(P)-1$ in the second branch; all these subtractions are in $\mathbb Z$. For the explicit function $\varphi\in F$, set $C_\varphi=\{P:\nu_P(\varphi)\ne0\ \lor\ 0<\nu_P(\varphi-1)\}$ and $b_\varphi(P)=\max\{0,-\nu_P(\varphi)\}$. The explicit Belyi hypothesis $h_\varphi$ means that $\varphi$ is transcendental over $\mathbb Q$ and, for every place $P$, $1<e_\varphi(P)$ implies $P\in C_\varphi$. Thus $\varphi\ne0,1$. The explicit finiteness proof $h_{\mathrm{fin}}$ states that this very set $C_\varphi$ is finite; it supplies the reduced divisor $C=\sum_{Q\in C_\varphi}[Q]$, where $[Q]$ has coefficient $1$ at $Q$ and $0$ elsewhere. In particular $C(P)=1$ on $C_\varphi$ and $C(P)=0$ outside it, using the supplied finite-support proof. The explicit canonical-divisor datum $\mathcal K$ supplies an integer-valued finitely supported divisor $D$ on all these places together with the equality $D(P)=a_u(P)$ for every $P$; this fixes its actual coefficients at regular places and at poles of $u$. Then there exists $r\in F$ such that $r\ne0$ and $D(P)+C(P)=b_\varphi(P)+\nu_P(r)$ for every place $P$. Thus the difference between this supplied $D$ plus this reduced cusp divisor and the actual polar divisor of $\varphi$ is the principal divisor of one nonzero rational function, with the positive sign shown in the equality. The same single $r$ works at all places, including all poles of $u$ and $\varphi$; no place is excluded and no uniqueness of $r$ is asserted.

**简体中文**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.canonicalCuspPolarLinearEquivalence`

设隐式参数为自然数 $N\in\mathbb N$，显式给定模型 $M$：它包含固定代数闭包 $\Omega=\overline{\mathbb Q(T)}$ 中的中间域 $\mathbb Q\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$、元素 $u,v\in F$，以及以下性质的证明：$u$ 在 $\mathbb Q$ 上超越，$u^N+v^N=1$，$\mathbb Q(u,v)=F$，且 $F/\mathbb Q(u)$ 为次数等于 $N$ 的有限维扩张。声明没有另加 $N$ 的下界条件；上述模型条件不能在 $N=0$ 时成立。这里的处 $P$ 遍历所有含 $\mathbb Q$ 的真赋值子环 $O_P\subsetneq F$，其剩余域记为 $\kappa(P)=O_P/\mathfrak m_P$，剩余映射记为 $\rho_P$。显式前提 $h_{\mathrm{DVR}}$ 要求每个 $O_P$ 都是离散赋值环，显式前提 $h_{\mathrm{RF}}$ 要求每个 $\kappa(P)$ 在 $\mathbb Q$ 上有限维。令 $\nu_P(f)$ 表示由 $O_P$ 的极大理想给出的规范化离散赋值取离散对数再取负得到的整数阶数，该赋值的值群为整数加法群的乘法记法副本并添入零元，并采用全函数约定 $\nu_P(0)=0$。对任意 $f\in F$，若 $f\in O_P$，令 $e_f(P)=\nu_P(m_{\rho_P(f)}(f))$，其中 $m_{\rho_P(f)}\in\mathbb Q[X]$ 为 $f$ 的剩余类在 $\mathbb Q$ 上的最小多项式；若 $f\notin O_P$，令 $e_f(P)=-\nu_P(f)$。前一分支定义 $a_f(P)=e_f(P)-1$，后一分支定义 $a_f(P)=-e_f(P)-1$；这些减法均在整数中进行。 对显式给定的函数 $\varphi\in F$，令 $C_\varphi=\{P:\nu_P(\varphi)\ne0\ \lor\ 0<\nu_P(\varphi-1)\}$，并令 $b_\varphi(P)=\max\{0,-\nu_P(\varphi)\}$。显式的 Belyi 条件 $h_\varphi$ 表示：$\varphi$ 在 $\mathbb Q$ 上超越，且对每个处 $P$，若 $1<e_\varphi(P)$，则 $P\in C_\varphi$。因此 $\varphi\ne0,1$。显式给定的有限性证明 $h_{\mathrm{fin}}$ 要求这个集合 $C_\varphi$ 本身有限，并由此构成约化除子 $C=\sum_{Q\in C_\varphi}[Q]$，其中 $[Q]$ 在 $Q$ 处的系数为 $1$，其他处的系数为 $0$。所以 $C(P)$ 在 $C_\varphi$ 上等于 $1$，在其外等于 $0$；该除子使用所给的有限支集证明。 显式给定的典范除子数据 $\mathcal K$ 包含定义在上述全部处上的有限支集整数值除子 $D$，以及对每个 $P$ 成立的等式 $D(P)=a_u(P)$；该条件固定了 $u$ 的正则处和极点处的实际系数。 那么存在 $r\in F$，使得 $r\ne0$，并且对每个处 $P$ 都有 $D(P)+C(P)=b_\varphi(P)+\nu_P(r)$。也就是说，所给除子 $D$ 加上这个约化尖点除子，与 $\varphi$ 的实际极除子之差，是同一个非零有理函数的主除子，符号为等式中所示的正号。同一个 $r$ 同时适用于全部处，包括 $u$ 和 $\varphi$ 的所有极点；没有排除任何处，也没有断言 $r$ 唯一。

**日本語**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.canonicalCuspPolarLinearEquivalence`

暗黙の引数を自然数 $N\in\mathbb N$ とし、明示的な模型 $M$ は、固定した代数閉包 $\Omega=\overline{\mathbb Q(T)}$ の中間体 $\mathbb Q\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$、元 $u,v\in F$、および $u$ が $\mathbb Q$ 上超越的であること、$u^N+v^N=1$、$\mathbb Q(u,v)=F$、$F/\mathbb Q(u)$ が次数 $N$ の有限次元拡大であることの証明からなるものとする。$N$ の下限について別の仮定はないが、これらの模型条件は $N=0$ では成立しない。素点 $P$ は、$\mathbb Q$ を含む真の付値部分環 $O_P\subsetneq F$ のすべてを動き、剰余体と剰余写像をそれぞれ $\kappa(P)=O_P/\mathfrak m_P$、$\rho_P$ と書く。明示的な仮定 $h_{\mathrm{DVR}}$ はすべての $O_P$ が離散付値環であることを、明示的な仮定 $h_{\mathrm{RF}}$ はすべての $\kappa(P)$ が $\mathbb Q$ 上有限次元であることを表す。$\nu_P(f)$ は $O_P$ の極大イデアルから得られる正規化された離散付値の離散対数の負値で定まる整数の位数であり、その付値の値群は整数の加法群を乗法的に書いたものに零元を付加したものであり、全域で定義するため $\nu_P(0)=0$ とする。任意の $f\in F$ に対して、$f\in O_P$ ならば $e_f(P)=\nu_P(m_{\rho_P(f)}(f))$ と定める。ただし $m_{\rho_P(f)}\in\mathbb Q[X]$ は $f$ の剰余類の $\mathbb Q$ 上の最小多項式である。$f\notin O_P$ ならば $e_f(P)=-\nu_P(f)$ と定める。前者では $a_f(P)=e_f(P)-1$、後者では $a_f(P)=-e_f(P)-1$ とし、これらの減算はすべて整数における減算である。 明示的に与えられた関数 $\varphi\in F$ に対して $C_\varphi=\{P:\nu_P(\varphi)\ne0\ \lor\ 0<\nu_P(\varphi-1)\}$ および $b_\varphi(P)=\max\{0,-\nu_P(\varphi)\}$ とおく。明示的な Belyi 条件 $h_\varphi$ は、$\varphi$ が $\mathbb Q$ 上超越的であり、すべての素点 $P$ について $1<e_\varphi(P)$ ならば $P\in C_\varphi$ となることを表す。したがって $\varphi\ne0,1$ である。明示的な有限性の証明 $h_{\mathrm{fin}}$ は、この集合 $C_\varphi$ 自体が有限であることを表し、これによって被約因子 $C=\sum_{Q\in C_\varphi}[Q]$ を定める。ここで $[Q]$ の係数は $Q$ で $1$、それ以外で $0$ である。従って $C(P)$ は $C_\varphi$ 上で $1$、その外で $0$ であり、この因子は与えられた有限台の証明を用いて構成される。 明示的な標準因子のデータ $\mathcal K$ は、これらすべての素点上の有限台をもつ整数値因子 $D$ と、各 $P$ に対する等式 $D(P)=a_u(P)$ からなる。この等式は $u$ が正則である素点でも極をもつ素点でも、その実際の係数を指定する。 このとき $r\in F$ が存在して、$r\ne0$ かつすべての素点 $P$ で $D(P)+C(P)=b_\varphi(P)+\nu_P(r)$ が成立する。従って、与えられた $D$ とこの被約カスプ因子の和から $\varphi$ の実際の極因子を引いた差は、ある一つの非零有理関数の主因子であり、その符号は等式に示す正符号である。同一の $r$ がすべての素点で成立し、$u$ と $\varphi$ のすべての極も含む。除外される素点はなく、$r$ の一意性は主張しない。

nodes.theorem_title: Actual Fermat points, heights and precise arithmetic inputs
nodes.natural_language_statement:
> “Since every point of $U_X(\overline{\mathbb Q})^{\le d}$ clearly lifts to a point of $U_Y(\overline{\mathbb Q})^{\le d^{\prime}}$, this completes the verification of the claim.”

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position*, proof of Theorem 2.1, printed p.12.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Pt`

For every natural number $N$, including $0$, this defines the type of ordered pairs $(a,b)$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of the rational field such that $a^N+b^N=1$, $a\ne0$, and $b\ne0$. There is no identification of different pairs and no additional restriction on $N$. For $N=0$ the equation is $1+1=1$, so this type has no elements.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.fieldOf`

For every natural number $N$ and every ordered pair $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,2}$ satisfying $a^N+b^N=1$, $a\ne0$, and $b\ne0$, this defines $K_p=\mathbb Q(a,b)$: the smallest intermediate field between $\mathbb Q$ and its fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ that contains both $a$ and $b$. The parameter $N$ has no positivity assumption; for $N=0$ there is no admissible $p$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.degree`

For every natural number $N$ and every ordered pair $p=(a,b)$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$ with $a^N+b^N=1$, $a\ne0$, and $b\ne0$, this defines a natural number $d_p$ as the dimension of $K_p=\mathbb Q(a,b)$ as a vector space over $\mathbb Q$, that is, $d_p=[\mathbb Q(a,b):\mathbb Q]$. The generated field is finite dimensional, and its degree is positive. No positivity assumption on $N$ is imposed; for $N=0$ there is no admissible $p$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.u`

For every natural number $N$ and every ordered pair $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,2}$ with $a^N+b^N=1$, $a\ne0$, and $b\ne0$, this defines $u_p$ to be the element of $K_p=\mathbb Q(a,b)$ whose underlying element in the fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ is the first coordinate $a$; its membership in $K_p$ is part of the construction. There is no positivity assumption on $N$; for $N=0$ there is no admissible $p$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.v`

For every natural number $N$ and every ordered pair $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,2}$ with $a^N+b^N=1$, $a\ne0$, and $b\ne0$, this defines $v_p$ to be the element of $K_p=\mathbb Q(a,b)$ whose underlying element in the fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ is the second coordinate $b$; its membership in $K_p$ is part of the construction. There is no positivity assumption on $N$; for $N=0$ there is no admissible $p$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.toTripod`

For every natural number $N$ and every ordered pair $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,2}$ satisfying $a^N+b^N=1$, $a\ne0$, and $b\ne0$, this defines an element of the type of algebraic numbers $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with $z\ne0$ and $z\ne1$: the chosen number is $z=a^N$. The construction includes proofs that $a^N\ne0$ and $a^N\ne1$. No positivity assumption on $N$ is imposed; for $N=0$ the domain has no elements.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.fieldOf_toTripod_le`

For every natural number $N$ and every ordered pair $p=(a,b)$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$ satisfying $a^N+b^N=1$, $a\ne0$, and $b\ne0$, the intermediate field generated over $\mathbb Q$ by the algebraic number $a^N$ is contained in the intermediate field generated by both coordinates: $\mathbb Q(a^N)\subseteq\mathbb Q(a,b)$. This is field inclusion inside the same algebraic closure, with equality allowed. There is no positivity assumption on $N$; for $N=0$ there is no admissible $p$ and the universal assertion has no instances.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.logDiff`

For every natural number $N$ and every ordered pair $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,2}$ with $a^N+b^N=1$, $a\ne0$, and $b\ne0$, let $K=\mathbb Q(a,b)$ and $d=[K:\mathbb Q]$. This defines the real number $\log|\operatorname{disc}(K)|/d$, where $\operatorname{disc}(K)$ is the integer number-field discriminant, viewed as a real number before taking its absolute value, and $\log$ is the natural logarithm. Here $d$ is viewed as a real number in the division; $d>0$ and the discriminant is nonzero, so neither division by zero nor the logarithm of zero occurs for an admissible $p$. No positivity assumption on $N$ is imposed; for $N=0$ there is no admissible $p$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.projectiveHeight`

For every natural number $N$ and every ordered pair $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,2}$ with $a^N+b^N=1$, $a\ne0$, and $b\ne0$, let $K=\mathbb Q(a,b)$ and $d=[K:\mathbb Q]$. This defines the real number $H_K(a,b,1)/d$, where $H_K(a,b,1)$ denotes the imported mathematical library's logarithmic height of the three-coordinate vector $(a,b,1)$ with all three coordinates regarded as elements of $K$; thus the coordinates are $a$, $b$, and $1$, without raising either coordinate to the power $N$. The natural number $d$ is viewed as a real number and is positive, so the denominator is nonzero. No positivity assumption on $N$ is imposed; for $N=0$ there is no admissible $p$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.canonicalHeight`

For every natural number $N$ and every ordered pair $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,2}$ with $a^N+b^N=1$, $a\ne0$, and $b\ne0$, let $K=\mathbb Q(a,b)$ and $d=[K:\mathbb Q]$. This defines the real number $(N-3)H_K(a,b,1)/d$, where $H_K(a,b,1)$ is the imported mathematical library's logarithmic height of the three-coordinate vector $(a,b,1)$ regarded as a vector over $K$, and $d$ is viewed as a real number. The subtraction $N-3$ is real subtraction after converting $N$ to a real number, not truncated natural-number subtraction. No assumption $N>3$ is made: the factors for $N=1,2,3$ are respectively $-2,-1,0$, with the whole value zero for $N=3$; $N=0$ has no admissible $p$. For every admissible $p$, $d>0$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.coefficient`

This defines a real-valued function of every natural number $N$ by $a_N=(N-3)/N$: subtraction and division take place in $\mathbb R$, not in $\mathbb N$. Real division is total, so the included case $N=0$ has value $0$; for $N=1,2,3$ the values are respectively $-2,-\tfrac12,0$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.HeightNormalization`

Let $\Omega=\overline{\mathbb Q}$ be the specified algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q$, and let $X=\Omega\setminus\{0,1\}$. For $z\in X$, put $K_z=\mathbb Q(z)$ and $n_z=[K_z:\mathbb Q]$, equivalently the degree of the minimal polynomial of $z$; this is positive. Let $h_K(t)$ denote the one-variable logarithmic height of $t$ computed in the number field $K$, and put $h(z)=h_{K_z}(z)/n_z$. For a natural number $N$, let $Y_N=\{(u,v)\in\Omega^2:u^N+v^N=1,\ u\ne0,\ v\ne0\}$. For $p=(u,v)\in Y_N$, set $L_p=\mathbb Q(u,v)$, $m_p=[L_p:\mathbb Q]>0$, and $q_N(p)=u^N\in X$. Let $H_L([u:v:1])$ be the logarithmic projective height of the three coordinates, computed in $L$, and set $\kappa_N(p)=(N-3)H_{L_p}([u:v:1])/m_p$, with subtraction in $\mathbb R$. Write $a_N=(N-3)/N$, with $N$ cast to $\mathbb R$ before subtraction and division. The proposition is: For every natural number $N>3$, there exists a real constant $C$, depending on $N$ but not on $p$, such that every $p\in Y_N$ satisfies $|\kappa_N(p)-a_Nh(q_N(p))|\le C$. The constant is not required in advance to be nonnegative. 

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.LiftDifferent`

Let $\Omega=\overline{\mathbb Q}$ be the specified algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q$, and let $X=\Omega\setminus\{0,1\}$. For $z\in X$, put $K_z=\mathbb Q(z)$ and $n_z=[K_z:\mathbb Q]$, equivalently the degree of the minimal polynomial of $z$; this is positive. Let $h_K(t)$ denote the one-variable logarithmic height of $t$ computed in the number field $K$, and put $h(z)=h_{K_z}(z)/n_z$. Write $D(z)=\log|\operatorname{disc}(K_z)|/n_z$ and $R(z)=n_z^{-1}\sum_{v:\,|z|_v\ne1\,\lor\,|z-1|_v\ne1}\log\operatorname N(\mathfrak p_v)$, where the sum runs over the finite places of $K_z$ satisfying the displayed condition, $|\cdot|_v$ is that place's absolute value, $\mathfrak p_v$ is its maximal ideal in the ring of integers, and $\operatorname N$ is absolute ideal norm. The sum has finite support. For a natural number $N$, let $Y_N=\{(u,v)\in\Omega^2:u^N+v^N=1,\ u\ne0,\ v\ne0\}$. For $p=(u,v)\in Y_N$, set $L_p=\mathbb Q(u,v)$, $m_p=[L_p:\mathbb Q]>0$, and $q_N(p)=u^N\in X$. Put $D_Y(p)=\log|\operatorname{disc}(L_p)|/m_p$, where $\operatorname{disc}$ denotes the number-field discriminant. The proposition is: For every natural number $N>0$, including $N=1$, there exists a real constant $C$, depending on $N$ but not on $z$, such that for every $z\in X$ there exists $p\in Y_N$ with $q_N(p)=z$, $m_p\le N^2n_z$, and $D_Y(p)\le D(z)+R(z)+C$. The point $p$ is not asserted to be unique, and no sign restriction is imposed on $C$. 

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.CanonicalEstimate`

Let $\Omega=\overline{\mathbb Q}$ be the specified algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q$, and let $X=\Omega\setminus\{0,1\}$. For $z\in X$, put $K_z=\mathbb Q(z)$ and $n_z=[K_z:\mathbb Q]$, equivalently the degree of the minimal polynomial of $z$; this is positive. Let $h_K(t)$ denote the one-variable logarithmic height of $t$ computed in the number field $K$, and put $h(z)=h_{K_z}(z)/n_z$. Write $D(z)=\log|\operatorname{disc}(K_z)|/n_z$ and $R(z)=n_z^{-1}\sum_{v:\,|z|_v\ne1\,\lor\,|z-1|_v\ne1}\log\operatorname N(\mathfrak p_v)$, where the sum runs over the finite places of $K_z$ satisfying the displayed condition, $|\cdot|_v$ is that place's absolute value, $\mathfrak p_v$ is its maximal ideal in the ring of integers, and $\operatorname N$ is absolute ideal norm. The sum has finite support. For each finite set $S$ of natural-number primes containing $2$ and each real $c$, let $E_{S,c}(z)$ mean that $|\log|z|_v|\le c$ and $|\log|z-1|_v|\le c$ for every finite place $v$ of $K_z$ whose residue field has characteristic in $S$, and also $|\log|z|_w|\le c$ and $|\log|z-1|_w|\le c$ for every infinite place $w$ of $K_z$. There is no sign restriction on $c$. Let $\mathcal B$ be the assertion that for every $b\in\mathbb N$, every real $\eta>0$, every such $S$, and every $c\in\mathbb R$, there exists $B\in\mathbb R$ such that every $z\in X$ with $E_{S,c}(z)$ and $n_z\le b$ satisfies $h(z)\le(1+\eta)(D(z)+R(z))+B$. The constant may depend on $b,\eta,S,c$ but not on $z$; $b=0$ and empty sets of eligible points are included. For a natural number $N$, let $Y_N=\{(u,v)\in\Omega^2:u^N+v^N=1,\ u\ne0,\ v\ne0\}$. For $p=(u,v)\in Y_N$, set $L_p=\mathbb Q(u,v)$, $m_p=[L_p:\mathbb Q]>0$, and $q_N(p)=u^N\in X$. Let $H_L([u:v:1])$ be the logarithmic projective height of the three coordinates, computed in $L$, and set $\kappa_N(p)=(N-3)H_{L_p}([u:v:1])/m_p$, with subtraction in $\mathbb R$. Put $D_Y(p)=\log|\operatorname{disc}(L_p)|/m_p$, where $\operatorname{disc}$ denotes the number-field discriminant. The proposition is that $\mathcal B$ implies the following: For every natural number $N>3$, every $d\in\mathbb N$, and every real $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a real constant $C$, depending on $N,d,\varepsilon$ but not on $p$, such that every $p\in Y_N$ with $m_p\le d$ satisfies $\kappa_N(p)\le(1+\varepsilon)D_Y(p)+C$. The case $d=0$ is included and has no eligible points; $C$ has no prescribed sign. 

**简体中文**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Pt`

对每个自然数 $N$（包括 $0$），此定义给出由有理数域的一个固定代数闭包 $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ 中的有序对 $(a,b)$ 所组成的类型，条件是 $a^N+b^N=1$、$a\ne0$ 且 $b\ne0$。不同有序对之间不作等同，也没有对 $N$ 的其他限制。当 $N=0$ 时，方程为 $1+1=1$，因此该类型没有元素。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.fieldOf`

对每个自然数 $N$ 以及每个满足 $a^N+b^N=1$、$a\ne0$、$b\ne0$ 的有序对 $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,2}$，此定义给出 $K_p=\mathbb Q(a,b)$，即有理数域 $\mathbb Q$ 与其固定代数闭包 $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ 之间同时包含 $a$ 和 $b$ 的最小中间域。参数 $N$ 无须为正；当 $N=0$ 时，没有满足条件的 $p$。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.degree`

对每个自然数 $N$ 以及有理数域 $\mathbb Q$ 的一个固定代数闭包 $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ 中每个满足 $a^N+b^N=1$、$a\ne0$、$b\ne0$ 的有序对 $p=(a,b)$，此定义把自然数 $d_p$ 定为域 $K_p=\mathbb Q(a,b)$ 作为 $\mathbb Q$ 上向量空间的维数，即 $d_p=[\mathbb Q(a,b):\mathbb Q]$。该生成域是有限维的，其次数为正。不要求 $N$ 为正；当 $N=0$ 时，没有满足条件的 $p$。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.u`

对每个自然数 $N$ 以及每个满足 $a^N+b^N=1$、$a\ne0$、$b\ne0$ 的有序对 $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,2}$，此定义给出域 $K_p=\mathbb Q(a,b)$ 中的元素 $u_p$，它在固定代数闭包 $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ 中的底层元素就是第一坐标 $a$；它属于 $K_p$ 的证明也包含在构造中。不要求 $N$ 为正；当 $N=0$ 时，没有满足条件的 $p$。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.v`

对每个自然数 $N$ 以及每个满足 $a^N+b^N=1$、$a\ne0$、$b\ne0$ 的有序对 $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,2}$，此定义给出域 $K_p=\mathbb Q(a,b)$ 中的元素 $v_p$，它在固定代数闭包 $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ 中的底层元素就是第二坐标 $b$；它属于 $K_p$ 的证明也包含在构造中。不要求 $N$ 为正；当 $N=0$ 时，没有满足条件的 $p$。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.toTripod`

对每个自然数 $N$ 以及每个满足 $a^N+b^N=1$、$a\ne0$、$b\ne0$ 的有序对 $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,2}$，此定义给出满足 $z\ne0$ 且 $z\ne1$ 的代数数 $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}$ 所组成的类型中的一个元素：所取的数为 $z=a^N$。构造包含 $a^N\ne0$ 和 $a^N\ne1$ 的证明。不要求 $N$ 为正；当 $N=0$ 时，定义域没有元素。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.logDiff`

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.projectiveHeight`

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.canonicalHeight`

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.coefficient`

此定义以每个自然数 $N$ 为自变量的实值函数 $a_N=(N-3)/N$：先将 $N$ 视为实数，再在实数域中作减法和除法，而不作自然数减法。实数除法对所有输入均有定义，因此包含的 $N=0$ 情形取值为 $0$；$N=1,2,3$ 时的值依次为 $-2,-\tfrac12,0$。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.HeightNormalization`

设 $\Omega=\overline{\mathbb Q}$ 为所指定的有理数域的代数闭包，$X=\Omega\setminus\{0,1\}$。对 $z\in X$，置 $K_z=\mathbb Q(z)$、$n_z=[K_z:\mathbb Q]$；后者也就是 $z$ 的最小多项式的次数，且为正。以 $h_K(t)$ 表示在数域 $K$ 中计算的元素 $t$ 的单变量对数高度，并置 $h(z)=h_{K_z}(z)/n_z$。对自然数 $N$，令 $Y_N=\{(u,v)\in\Omega^2:u^N+v^N=1,\ u\ne0,\ v\ne0\}$。对 $p=(u,v)\in Y_N$，置 $L_p=\mathbb Q(u,v)$、$m_p=[L_p:\mathbb Q]>0$，并令 $q_N(p)=u^N\in X$。以 $H_L([u:v:1])$ 表示在数域 $L$ 中计算的这三个坐标的对数射影高度，并置 $\kappa_N(p)=(N-3)H_{L_p}([u:v:1])/m_p$，其中减法在实数域中进行。记 $a_N=(N-3)/N$，其中先将 $N$ 视为实数，再作减法和除法。其命题为：对每个自然数 $N>3$，存在可以依赖 $N$ 但不依赖 $p$ 的实常数 $C$，使每个 $p\in Y_N$ 都满足 $|\kappa_N(p)-a_Nh(q_N(p))|\le C$。不预先要求该常数非负。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.LiftDifferent`

设 $\Omega=\overline{\mathbb Q}$ 为所指定的有理数域的代数闭包，$X=\Omega\setminus\{0,1\}$。对 $z\in X$，置 $K_z=\mathbb Q(z)$、$n_z=[K_z:\mathbb Q]$；后者也就是 $z$ 的最小多项式的次数，且为正。以 $h_K(t)$ 表示在数域 $K$ 中计算的元素 $t$ 的单变量对数高度，并置 $h(z)=h_{K_z}(z)/n_z$。记 $D(z)=\log|\operatorname{disc}(K_z)|/n_z$，其中 $\operatorname{disc}(K_z)$ 为数域判别式；又记 $R(z)=n_z^{-1}\sum_{v:\,|z|_v\ne1\,\lor\,|z-1|_v\ne1}\log\operatorname N(\mathfrak p_v)$，求和遍历 $K_z$ 中满足所示条件的有限位，$|\cdot|_v$ 为该位的绝对值，$\mathfrak p_v$ 为其在整数环中对应的极大理想，$\operatorname N$ 为理想的绝对范数。此和只有有限多个非零项。对自然数 $N$，令 $Y_N=\{(u,v)\in\Omega^2:u^N+v^N=1,\ u\ne0,\ v\ne0\}$。对 $p=(u,v)\in Y_N$，置 $L_p=\mathbb Q(u,v)$、$m_p=[L_p:\mathbb Q]>0$，并令 $q_N(p)=u^N\in X$。置 $D_Y(p)=\log|\operatorname{disc}(L_p)|/m_p$，其中 $\operatorname{disc}$ 表示数域判别式。其命题为：对每个自然数 $N>0$，包括 $N=1$，存在可以依赖 $N$ 但不依赖 $z$ 的实常数 $C$，使对每个 $z\in X$，都存在 $p\in Y_N$，同时满足 $q_N(p)=z$、$m_p\le N^2n_z$ 及 $D_Y(p)\le D(z)+R(z)+C$。不要求 $p$ 唯一，对 $C$ 不作符号限制。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.CanonicalEstimate`

设 $\Omega=\overline{\mathbb Q}$ 为所指定的有理数域的代数闭包，$X=\Omega\setminus\{0,1\}$。对 $z\in X$，置 $K_z=\mathbb Q(z)$、$n_z=[K_z:\mathbb Q]$；后者也就是 $z$ 的最小多项式的次数，且为正。以 $h_K(t)$ 表示在数域 $K$ 中计算的元素 $t$ 的单变量对数高度，并置 $h(z)=h_{K_z}(z)/n_z$。记 $D(z)=\log|\operatorname{disc}(K_z)|/n_z$，其中 $\operatorname{disc}(K_z)$ 为数域判别式；又记 $R(z)=n_z^{-1}\sum_{v:\,|z|_v\ne1\,\lor\,|z-1|_v\ne1}\log\operatorname N(\mathfrak p_v)$，求和遍历 $K_z$ 中满足所示条件的有限位，$|\cdot|_v$ 为该位的绝对值，$\mathfrak p_v$ 为其在整数环中对应的极大理想，$\operatorname N$ 为理想的绝对范数。此和只有有限多个非零项。对每个包含 $2$ 且其元素均为素数的自然数有限集 $S$ 及每个实数 $c$，以 $E_{S,c}(z)$ 表示如下条件：对 $K_z$ 中每个剩余域的特征属于 $S$ 的有限位 $v$，均有 $|\log|z|_v|\le c$ 且 $|\log|z-1|_v|\le c$；对 $K_z$ 中每个无限位 $w$，也均有 $|\log|z|_w|\le c$ 且 $|\log|z-1|_w|\le c$。对 $c$ 不作符号限制。以 $\mathcal B$ 表示以下断言：对每个 $b\in\mathbb N$、每个实数 $\eta>0$、每个这样的 $S$ 和每个 $c\in\mathbb R$，存在 $B\in\mathbb R$，使每个满足 $E_{S,c}(z)$ 及 $n_z\le b$ 的 $z\in X$ 都满足 $h(z)\le(1+\eta)(D(z)+R(z))+B$。常数可以依赖 $b,\eta,S,c$，但不依赖 $z$；量词包括 $b=0$ 及合格点集为空的情形。对自然数 $N$，令 $Y_N=\{(u,v)\in\Omega^2:u^N+v^N=1,\ u\ne0,\ v\ne0\}$。对 $p=(u,v)\in Y_N$，置 $L_p=\mathbb Q(u,v)$、$m_p=[L_p:\mathbb Q]>0$，并令 $q_N(p)=u^N\in X$。以 $H_L([u:v:1])$ 表示在数域 $L$ 中计算的这三个坐标的对数射影高度，并置 $\kappa_N(p)=(N-3)H_{L_p}([u:v:1])/m_p$，其中减法在实数域中进行。置 $D_Y(p)=\log|\operatorname{disc}(L_p)|/m_p$，其中 $\operatorname{disc}$ 表示数域判别式。其命题为 $\mathcal B$ 蕴含以下断言：对每个自然数 $N>3$、每个 $d\in\mathbb N$ 及每个实数 $\varepsilon>0$，存在可以依赖 $N,d,\varepsilon$ 但不依赖 $p$ 的实常数 $C$，使每个满足 $m_p\le d$ 的 $p\in Y_N$ 都满足 $\kappa_N(p)\le(1+\varepsilon)D_Y(p)+C$。包括 $d=0$ 的情形，此时没有合格点；对 $C$ 不作符号限制。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Pt`

各自然数 $N$ および $a^N+b^N=1$、$a\ne0$、$b\ne0$ を満たす各順序対 $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,2}$ に対して、体 $K_p=\mathbb Q(a,b)$ の要素 $u_p$ を定義する。その固定された代数閉包 $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ における基礎となる要素は第一座標 $a$ であり、$K_p$ に属することの証明も構成に含まれる。$N$ が正であるという仮定はなく、$N=0$ の場合には条件を満たす $p$ は存在しない。

各自然数 $N$ および $a^N+b^N=1$、$a\ne0$、$b\ne0$ を満たす各順序対 $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,2}$ に対して、体 $K_p=\mathbb Q(a,b)$ の要素 $v_p$ を定義する。その固定された代数閉包 $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ における基礎となる要素は第二座標 $b$ であり、$K_p$ に属することの証明も構成に含まれる。$N$ が正であるという仮定はなく、$N=0$ の場合には条件を満たす $p$ は存在しない。

各自然数 $N$ および $a^N+b^N=1$、$a\ne0$、$b\ne0$ を満たす各順序対 $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,2}$ に対して、$K=\mathbb Q(a,b)$、$d=[K:\mathbb Q]$ とおく。この定義は実数 $\log|\operatorname{disc}(K)|/d$ を与える。ここで $\operatorname{disc}(K)$ は数体の整数判別式であり、実数とみなした後に絶対値を取り、$\log$ は自然対数を表す。除算では $d$ を実数とみなす。$d>0$ かつ判別式は零でないため、条件を満たす $p$ について零による除算や零の対数は生じない。$N$ が正であるという仮定はなく、$N=0$ の場合には条件を満たす $p$ は存在しない。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.HeightNormalization`

$\Omega=\overline{\mathbb Q}$ を指定された有理数体の代数閉包とし、$X=\Omega\setminus\{0,1\}$ とする。$z\in X$ に対して $K_z=\mathbb Q(z)$、$n_z=[K_z:\mathbb Q]$ と置く。後者は $z$ の最小多項式の次数に等しく、正である。$h_K(t)$ を数体 $K$ において計算する元 $t$ の一変数対数的高さとし、$h(z)=h_{K_z}(z)/n_z$ と置く。自然数 $N$ に対し、$Y_N=\{(u,v)\in\Omega^2:u^N+v^N=1,\ u\ne0,\ v\ne0\}$ とする。$p=(u,v)\in Y_N$ に対して $L_p=\mathbb Q(u,v)$、$m_p=[L_p:\mathbb Q]>0$、$q_N(p)=u^N\in X$ と置く。$H_L([u:v:1])$ を数体 $L$ において計算する三つの座標の対数的射影高さとし、$\kappa_N(p)=(N-3)H_{L_p}([u:v:1])/m_p$ と置く。ここで減法は実数上で行う。$a_N=(N-3)/N$ と書く。$N$ は減法と除法の前に実数とみなす。命題は次のとおりである。任意の自然数 $N>3$ に対し、$N$ に依存してよいが $p$ には依存しない実定数 $C$ が存在し、すべての $p\in Y_N$ について $|\kappa_N(p)-a_Nh(q_N(p))|\le C$ が成り立つ。定数に対してあらかじめ非負性は仮定しない。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.LiftDifferent`

$\Omega=\overline{\mathbb Q}$ を指定された有理数体の代数閉包とし、$X=\Omega\setminus\{0,1\}$ とする。$z\in X$ に対して $K_z=\mathbb Q(z)$、$n_z=[K_z:\mathbb Q]$ と置く。後者は $z$ の最小多項式の次数に等しく、正である。$h_K(t)$ を数体 $K$ において計算する元 $t$ の一変数対数的高さとし、$h(z)=h_{K_z}(z)/n_z$ と置く。$D(z)=\log|\operatorname{disc}(K_z)|/n_z$ と書く。ここで $\operatorname{disc}(K_z)$ は数体の判別式である。また $R(z)=n_z^{-1}\sum_{v:\,|z|_v\ne1\,\lor\,|z-1|_v\ne1}\log\operatorname N(\mathfrak p_v)$ とする。和は表示された条件を満たす $K_z$ の有限素点にわたり、$|\cdot|_v$ はその素点の絶対値、$\mathfrak p_v$ は整数環において対応する極大イデアル、$\operatorname N$ はイデアルの絶対ノルムである。この和の台は有限である。自然数 $N$ に対し、$Y_N=\{(u,v)\in\Omega^2:u^N+v^N=1,\ u\ne0,\ v\ne0\}$ とする。$p=(u,v)\in Y_N$ に対して $L_p=\mathbb Q(u,v)$、$m_p=[L_p:\mathbb Q]>0$、$q_N(p)=u^N\in X$ と置く。$D_Y(p)=\log|\operatorname{disc}(L_p)|/m_p$ と置く。ここで $\operatorname{disc}$ は数体の判別式を表す。命題は次のとおりである。$N=1$ を含む任意の自然数 $N>0$ に対し、$N$ に依存してよいが $z$ には依存しない実定数 $C$ が存在し、任意の $z\in X$ に対して $q_N(p)=z$、$m_p\le N^2n_z$、$D_Y(p)\le D(z)+R(z)+C$ を同時に満たす $p\in Y_N$ が存在する。$p$ の一意性は主張せず、$C$ の符号には制限を課さない。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.CanonicalEstimate`

$\Omega=\overline{\mathbb Q}$ を指定された有理数体の代数閉包とし、$X=\Omega\setminus\{0,1\}$ とする。$z\in X$ に対して $K_z=\mathbb Q(z)$、$n_z=[K_z:\mathbb Q]$ と置く。後者は $z$ の最小多項式の次数に等しく、正である。$h_K(t)$ を数体 $K$ において計算する元 $t$ の一変数対数的高さとし、$h(z)=h_{K_z}(z)/n_z$ と置く。$D(z)=\log|\operatorname{disc}(K_z)|/n_z$ と書く。ここで $\operatorname{disc}(K_z)$ は数体の判別式である。また $R(z)=n_z^{-1}\sum_{v:\,|z|_v\ne1\,\lor\,|z-1|_v\ne1}\log\operatorname N(\mathfrak p_v)$ とする。和は表示された条件を満たす $K_z$ の有限素点にわたり、$|\cdot|_v$ はその素点の絶対値、$\mathfrak p_v$ は整数環において対応する極大イデアル、$\operatorname N$ はイデアルの絶対ノルムである。この和の台は有限である。$2$ を含み、すべての元が素数である自然数の有限集合 $S$ と実数 $c$ に対して、$E_{S,c}(z)$ を次の条件とする。$K_z$ の有限素点 $v$ で、その剰余体の標数が $S$ に属するものすべてについて $|\log|z|_v|\le c$ かつ $|\log|z-1|_v|\le c$ が成り立ち、さらに $K_z$ のすべての無限素点 $w$ について $|\log|z|_w|\le c$ かつ $|\log|z-1|_w|\le c$ が成り立つ。$c$ の符号には制限がない。$\mathcal B$ を次の主張とする。任意の $b\in\mathbb N$、実数 $\eta>0$、上述の $S$、および $c\in\mathbb R$ に対し、ある $B\in\mathbb R$ が存在し、$E_{S,c}(z)$ と $n_z\le b$ を満たすすべての $z\in X$ について $h(z)\le(1+\eta)(D(z)+R(z))+B$ が成り立つ。定数は $b,\eta,S,c$ に依存してよいが、$z$ には依存しない。$b=0$ および該当する点の集合が空の場合も含まれる。自然数 $N$ に対し、$Y_N=\{(u,v)\in\Omega^2:u^N+v^N=1,\ u\ne0,\ v\ne0\}$ とする。$p=(u,v)\in Y_N$ に対して $L_p=\mathbb Q(u,v)$、$m_p=[L_p:\mathbb Q]>0$、$q_N(p)=u^N\in X$ と置く。$H_L([u:v:1])$ を数体 $L$ において計算する三つの座標の対数的射影高さとし、$\kappa_N(p)=(N-3)H_{L_p}([u:v:1])/m_p$ と置く。ここで減法は実数上で行う。$D_Y(p)=\log|\operatorname{disc}(L_p)|/m_p$ と置く。ここで $\operatorname{disc}$ は数体の判別式を表す。命題は、$\mathcal B$ が次の主張を含意するというものである。任意の自然数 $N>3$、$d\in\mathbb N$、および実数 $\varepsilon>0$ に対し、$N,d,\varepsilon$ に依存してよいが $p$ には依存しない実定数 $C$ が存在し、$m_p\le d$ を満たすすべての $p\in Y_N$ について $\kappa_N(p)\le(1+\varepsilon)D_Y(p)+C$ が成り立つ。$d=0$ も含まれ、この場合は該当する点がない。$C$ の符号には制限がない。

/-
